- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is high (≥0.65) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate when sentiment is low (≤0.3) — model is overly conservative, missing upward momentum.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts: if sentiment drops sharply, model doesn’t adjust downward quickly enough.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high after strong upward moves, ignoring recent volatility.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early in the period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is bullish, then undercorrect later.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.6), model tends to err on the side of caution — underestimating true volatility.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends if sentiment is diverging — e.g., if sentiment drops after a spike, model may still forecast upward.
